recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Editing the current source would either duplicate existing guidance or conflict with FHIR-20396's deliberate replacement of choice/open-choice with coding plus answerConstraint.
issue_request: The Published/Persuasive issue asked whether DSTU1 Questionnaire.group.question.type could represent a code, such as a dropdown value. The approved resolution said yes: the Choice type allowed coded data, and definitions would be added to all type codes to make this clear.
initial_application: The Jira comments record legacy application in SVN #5941. Current git history no longer exposes that SVN patch directly, but the migrated/current Questionnaire item type terminology already carries definitions for item type codes, and the inspected resource/value-set files are active build-scope source.
additional_context: FHIR-20396 later made a Published/Persuasive with Modification R5 change for the same item-type family: it removed choice/open-choice from Questionnaire.item.type, added coding, and moved list/off-list answer behavior into answerConstraint with answerOption and answerValueSet. Commit ae142a024a99c23b140a4d007595a8e3f1f06d52 applied that redesign, so the old Choice terminology should not be restored.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source defines Questionnaire.item.type as a required code bound to item-type-useable, identifies Coding as a captured data type, defines the coding item type as valueCoding generally drawn from possible answers, and explains permitted answer values through answerOption or answerValueSet.

related_jiras.note: Published R5 decision replacing choice/open-choice with coding plus answerConstraint, which controls how the older FHIR-6811 Choice resolution should be read in current source.
